Медь.about: Copper is an essential mineral, but there is no data on the benefits of supplementation at normal levels: ESPEN explicitly notes the lack of intervention studies.
Медь.caution: ESPEN specifically addresses the potential toxicity of micronutrients in excess; There is no data on the upper limit specifically for copper in the pool.
Медь.course: not specified; ESPEN describes monitoring micronutrient status during nutritional support
Медь.food_sources: Liver, seafood, nuts, seeds and cocoa; The Vegan Diet SR lists copper as one of the nutrients for which no deficiency has been identified.
Медь.guidelines: ESPEN 2022: Recommendations for micronutrients are based on consensus, there are few intervention studies, a meta-analysis could not be carried out - the level of evidence is low.
Медь.how_to_choose: Pool copper supplements are not supported by any research; if a deficiency is suspected, use a blood test rather than taking it on your own.
mechs: Copper is an essential trace element necessary for metabolism; deficiency is detected in acute and chronic diseases
Deficiency or imbalance of micronutrients is considered as a possible factor in the pathogenesis of androgenetic alopecia
There is no direct data on the effect of copper intake on a healthy person in the studies studied.
The effect of the supplement outside of deficiency has not been confirmed
Медь.myths: “Everyone needs copper” - SR on a vegan diet did not reveal any copper deficiency. “Improves hair growth” - in the SR on androgenetic alopecia, copper is only in the list of micronutrients, the conclusions relate to B, D, Fe, Se, Zn.
Медь.name: Copper
Медь.onset: Not studied: There are no separate RCTs measuring the timing of the copper effect in the pool.
Медь.title: Copper
Медь.who_needs: Only with confirmed deficiency or with enteral and parenteral nutrition. In a normal diet, copper deficiency has not been identified, even among vegans.
